# Results — Study 680 (Disparity Index)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test —
**DI(N) = 100 x Close / SMA(N)**, a Korean/Japanese-technical-analysis staple, flags
overbought/oversold extremes that mean-revert: DI < 95 ("stretched down 5%+") should buy,
DI > 105 ("stretched up 5%+") should sell/short, N = 10 the textbook short-horizon
default. Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to
reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month; the
partial current month is dropped). Fingerprints `c6509bba7177` (SPY) / `824e9d9be08f`
(QQQ) / `1a82f99e4745` (IWM) / `db335bf7a084` (AAPL) / `1d273fa4b475` (TSLA) /
`e3f7f5f85931` (NVDA).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily total-return-adjusted OHLC, SPY/QQQ/IWM/AAPL/NVDA 5,910 rows 2003-01-02 → 2026-06-30, TSLA 4,025 rows 2010-06-29 → 2026-06-30 (post-IPO) |
| Universe | SPY, QQQ, IWM (index ETFs, no survivorship) + AAPL, TSLA, NVDA (liquid, currently-thriving mega caps chosen for name recognition, **not** a systematic historical panel — named honestly; a 1999-vintage tech basket including the era's flame-outs would look different). Identical universe to sibling [679-psychological-line](../../679-psychological-line/) |
| Indicator | DI(window) = 100 x Close / trailing-window SMA; headline window = **10**, zone thresholds **oversold < 95, overbought > 105** (textbook short-horizon Korean-TA defaults); swept over windows {5,10,20,25} x threshold pairs {±3,±5,±7}% |
| Statistics | Welch *t* (planned primary) for the conditional split; Newey-West (HAC, *h*=5 lags) *t* as the overlap-robust cross-check on both the conditional split and the null-world power check; HAC(*h*) *t* on the trade ledgers |
| Execution / costs | one documented convention: DI known at the close of bar *t*; every trade enters at bar *t+1*'s **open**, exits at the close of *t+h−1* (*h* = 5 trading days); one round trip = 2 x one-way cost x NAV (5 / 10 bps swept); long the oversold trigger, short the overbought trigger, no borrow modeled beyond the cost sweep |
| Controls | (1) a random-**direction** coin on the identical entry bars (does the DI-implied sign beat a coin flip on the days it fires); (2) a random-**day**, same-ticker, same-direction baseline (does the surviving leg beat simply buying/shorting an arbitrary day of the same drifting stock) — the honest "just captured beta?" check; (3) a 20-seed synthetic faithful-engine control |

No survivorship on the index legs (SPY/QQQ/IWM); the single-name sleeve's mild
name-recognition selection is named above and does not affect the Signal verdict (the
result is driven by the pooled drift these names shared over 2003–2026, which the
drift-baseline control below neutralizes explicitly).

## The headline — forward return conditioned on the DI reading

| bucket | n | mean fwd return (5d) | Welch *t* vs neutral | NW(5) *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| oversold (DI < 95) | 1,825 | **+111.60 bps** | **+3.84** | **+2.50** |
| neutral | 29,406 | +38.16 bps | | |
| overbought (DI > 105) | 2,338 | **+99.64 bps** | **+4.30** | **+2.68** |

Both extremes beat the neutral bucket, and both clear *t* ≥ 2 on the real tape by the
letter of the inference bar — but **the overbought leg is the wrong sign**. The claim says
DI > 105 should predict *below-average* forward returns (sell the top); it predicts
**above-average** ones, just as strongly as the oversold leg. That is a momentum/drift
signature, not mean reversion — see the drift check below.

## The timer — a two-sided trade ledger (buy oversold, short overbought) vs a coin

Enter next open, hold 5 trading days, one round trip = 2 x one-way cost x NAV.

| cost | DI timer (n=4,163) | random-direction coin (n=4,163, same entries) |
|---|---|---|
| 5 bps | win 48.8%, **−17.03 bps/trade** (HAC *t* = −0.94) | win 49.1%, +0.87 bps/trade (HAC *t* = +0.07) |
| 10 bps | win 48.3%, −27.03 bps/trade (HAC *t* = −1.49) | win 48.5%, −9.13 bps/trade (HAC *t* = −0.75) |

**Delta (DI timer − coin) at 5 bps: −17.90 bps/trade, Welch *t* = −1.09.** Taken literally
— long the dip, short the rip, as the folklore prescribes — the strategy **loses money**
net of costs, and is statistically indistinguishable from (if anything slightly worse
than) flipping a coin on the same entry days. The short-overbought leg is actively
fighting the momentum documented above.

## The drift check — does the surviving leg beat plain buy-any-random-day?

Each single-sided leg vs a same-ticker, same-direction, same-size **random-day** entry
control (not a coin — a different calendar day entirely), at 5 bps.

| leg | n | mean net (HAC *t*) | random-day mean net (HAC *t*) | delta | Welch *t* of delta |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| buy-oversold (long) | 1,825 | +101.60 bps (*t* = +3.49) | +67.05 bps (*t* = +4.51) | **+34.55 bps** | **+1.42** |
| short-overbought | 2,338 | −109.64 bps (*t* = −4.87) | −91.32 bps (*t* = −6.73) | **−18.31 bps** | **−0.94** |

This is the decisive result. **Random days in the same six-ticker, 2003–2026 universe
are already profitable** (long +67 bps, HAC *t* = +4.51 — pure pooled drift, mostly NVDA
and TSLA) **and already unprofitable to short** (−91 bps). Once that drift is netted out,
neither DI leg beats its own random-day twin: buying the dip adds +34.55 bps at *t* =
**+1.42** (below the bar), and DI-timed shorting is *worse* than random shorting at *t* =
**−0.94**. The raw "oversold beats neutral" split above is real arithmetic — it is just
**not information**; it is the same bull-market drift a random entry on the same stock
collects for free.

## "Just short-term reversal?" diagnostic

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| pooled Pearson corr(DI(10) − 100, trailing 10-day return) | **r = 0.8366** (n = 33,515) |

DI is, by construction, a smoothed, near-monotonic transform of the trailing N-day
return (r = 0.84): a "rubber-band distance from a moving average" *is* an accumulated-
return measure wearing a different scale. Conditioning on DI extremes is mechanically
close to conditioning on plain trailing-return extremes — the exact object sibling study
[329-one-month-reversal](../../329-one-month-reversal/) already tested and found to be
**mostly bid-ask-bounce microstructure, dead since 2002** on the current S&P 500. The
"Disparity Index" is not a distinct discovery.

The "*t* high" column is **positive and grows with window length** across every cell of
the grid — the overbought-continues-up pattern is not a fluke of one threshold pair, it
is structural to the indicator on this pooled, drift-heavy universe. No parameter choice
recovers the "sell the overbought" half of the claim.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic random-walk-plus-planted-reversion tape, disparity computed causally
(no look-ahead); a 6-series basket per seed mirrors the real 6-ticker pooling. The 5-day
forward windows overlap, so a raw Welch *t* over-fires on a single autocorrelated path;
**Newey-West(5) is the calibrated detector** here (the same cross-check used on the
headline split).

| world | detector | *t* low | *t* high |
|---|---|--:|--:|
| null (reversal = 0), 20 seeds | Welch | mean −0.16 (sd 1.55), \|t\|≥2 in 5/20 | mean +0.09 (sd 1.27), \|t\|≥2 in 2/20 |
| null (reversal = 0), 20 seeds | **NW(5)** | **mean −0.08 (sd 1.25), \|t\|≥2 in 2/20** | **mean +0.06 (sd 0.99), \|t\|≥2 in 1/20** |
| planted reversal = +0.006/day (seed 680) | Welch / NW(5) | +3.88 / **+3.33** | −2.47 / **−2.09** |

Under the NW(5) detector the null fires close to the 5% nominal rate expected of a
two-sided *t* ≥ 2 test (2/20, 1/20), and a planted reversion lights up cleanly both ways
(*t* = +3.33 / −2.09). The engine is unbiased; the real-tape asymmetry (both legs
positive) is a genuine feature of the real data, not a detector artefact. *(Faithful-
engine / power check only — never cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** The raw conditional split clears *t* ≥ 2 on the real tape both ways
  (oversold +111.6 bps/5d, Welch *t* = +3.84, NW *t* = +2.50; overbought +99.6 bps/5d,
  Welch *t* = +4.30, NW *t* = +2.68) — but the overbought leg has the **wrong sign**
  versus the claim, and once compared to a same-ticker random-day baseline the surviving
  oversold leg's edge (+34.55 bps) falls to Welch *t* = +1.42 — below the bar. What
  looked like a signal is captured pooled drift; DI itself correlates r = 0.84 with the
  plain trailing return (i.e. it is [329-one-month-reversal](../../329-one-month-reversal/)
  relabeled, a sibling already shown to be microstructure, dead since 2002).
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The literal two-sided rule (buy oversold, short overbought)
  **loses money net of costs** (−17.03 bps/trade at 5 bps, HAC *t* = −0.94) and is not
  distinguishable from a random-direction coin on the same entries (delta *t* = −1.09).
  The short leg actively fights a real momentum effect.
- **"More than plain short-term reversal / drift?" — BUSTED.** DI is a smoothed
  transform of the trailing return (r = 0.84); the "oversold" leg does not beat buying an
  arbitrary day of the same drifting stock (*t* = +1.42), and the "overbought" leg is
  backwards. The rubber band is not snapping back — the stocks that ran hardest kept
  running.
